name: the single object made for one named person
function: It is made for somebody the maker knows, and given to them. There is one, there will never be another, and the person receiving it did not ask for it. They know the maker, which means they cannot receive it neutrally: they will read it as being about them, or about the two of them, whether or not it is. It then lives in that person's house for as long as they want it there, and the maker will keep seeing it.
consequences: There is exactly one viewer and they are known by name. Every general solution is available and every one of them is wrong, because a thing that would work for anybody was not made for this person and they can tell.
It cannot be taken back. Once given it is theirs, including the right to put it in a drawer, and the maker has to keep knowing the person while not knowing where it is.

The recipient will look for themselves in it. Anything that resembles a likeness, a private reference or a shared occasion will be found whether or not it was put there, and anything genuinely put there is a claim about the relationship that they now have to answer.

It arrives without being asked for, which makes it an imposition as well as a gift. It has to be a thing the maker is not embarrassed to hand over and the receiver is not obliged to display, and those two pull in opposite directions.
The maker will see it again, on their wall or not on their wall, for years. Every other kind of object goes away; this one comes back at dinner.

It is handled before it is looked at. It is passed from one pair of hands to another in a room with both people in it, and the first reading happens with the maker watching, at the worst possible distance and the worst possible moment.

It is one object, made once. There is no matrix, no run, no second attempt and no proof pulled to check. A mark that can only be made once is fully available here, and so is the risk of making it badly.
It outlives the relationship. It will still be in their house after a falling-out, a move, or a death, and it will be looked at by people who do not know who made it or why.
doesNotDecide: Composition, palette, imagery, type, scale, whether it is legible to anyone else, how much of the surface is used, whether the person is in it, and what it is about. None of that follows from there being one recipient.
